text.tspan: ID
Requirement
Statement
Source
Rationale
Method
Criteria
REQ-HMI-001
reqShowTheSceneAsGiven
The HMI display shall show, within the
presentation time, each scene that reaches
it outside an outage in the IVI VM, or a
newer scene, as the driver-assistance
system gives it.
NEED-HMI-001; hmiDisplayInputsConcern;
hmiContentVarianceConcern; scope item
hmiSceneInScope; gaps gapHmiSceneOutput
and gapHmiSceneContent; scenarios SC-
HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
The driver supervises the driver-
assistance system with what it perceives,
right or wrong, so the display shows the
scene that the system gives and no other.
At 014e0e7a the system builds a scene only
inside its own visualization, in a build
with the option ENABLE_OCCUPANCY and with
the visualization switched on
(visual_interface.cpp:645-648;
vision_pilot.cpp:177). The bridge of its
panel builds it from the lane points of
AutoSteer placed on the road through the
homography that the system loads, the path
that the lateral fusion fits, the offset
and the heading of the vehicle in its
lane, the detections of AutoSpeed as boxes
with a score and a class, and the validity
and the distance of the closest object,
and it does not read the plan
(occupancy_bridge.cpp:20-77). That scene
carries no speed of the closest object and
no time, and the inference result carries
a frame identity and no capture time
(occupancy_view.hpp:23-48;
inference.hpp:38-52). So the scene that
the display takes is an output that the
system does not give yet
(gapHmiSceneOutput), and what it carries
bounds what the display can show of it
(gapHmiSceneContent). The scene is the one
input whose form follows the driving
application, so this requirement and REQ-
HMI-002 follow it. The display may skip a
scene only for a newer one. The
presentation time bounds the delay, so
that a display that shows each scene late
cannot hide behind REQ-HMI-006. During an
outage in the IVI VM the app that draws
the scene cannot show it; REQ-HMI-006 then
shows the scene as outdated, and once the
app gives its first frame again this
requirement holds again. A display that
shows the simulator's record of the scene
or an estimate of its own shows another
scene (hmiSimulatorTruthOutOfScope).
test
Met when each of SC-HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
has at least one run, each run of SC-
HMI-004 and SC-HMI-006 has the end of its
outage in the IVI VM before its own end,
and in each run every scene that reaches
the HMI display outside an outage in the
IVI VM, or a newer scene, is on the
display less than 0.1 s of wall-clock time
after it arrives, with its lane points,
its path and each of its objects with its
level, as many objects as the scene gives
and at the positions that it gives, read
within the drawing tolerance that phase 8
states; and when no frame on the display
shows a lane, a path or an object that no
scene of the run gives, from the
simulator's record of the scene or from an
estimate of the display's own.
REQ-HMI-002
reqMarkTheObjectTheSystemActsOn
With each scene that it shows, the HMI
display shall show the object that the
system acts on, when the scene has one,
and no other object, as an element of its
own apart from the objects of the scene,
with its distance to the whole metre and
the speed of the closest object to the
whole km/h.
NEED-HMI-001; scope item hmiSceneInScope;
gap gapHmiSceneContent; scenarios SC-
HMI-001 and SC-HMI-002
NEED-HMI-001 asks for the closest object
in the path, which the system acts on,
marked apart from the other objects. At
014e0e7a the fusion takes as the closest
object the nearest detection of the first
level, or of the second when that one is
nearer, a cut-in
(longitudinal_fusion.cpp:181-182,
207-210), and fuses its distance with the
distance that AutoDrive gives where
AutoDrive flags an object in the path.
Where AutoSpeed gives no detection of the
first level and AutoDrive flags no object
in the path, the fusion still gives a
valid closest object at a fixed distance
of 150 m (longitudinal_fusion.cpp:56,
63-73), and the system plans on the
closest object only when it is valid and
nearer than 150 m
(vision_pilot.cpp:147-150). So the object
that the system acts on is that one, and
no object is marked at the fixed distance.
The value of 150 m is compared when the
pin moves, and a change revises the term.
The scene names no detection as the
closest object, so the display shows that
object as an element of its own and marks
no detection as it: choosing a box would
be an estimate of the display's own. The
fusion gives the distance in m and the
speed in m/s, negative when the object
approaches, as its own declaration states
(longitudinal_fusion.hpp:17-18); the
display shows that speed with its sign, in
km/h. The whole metre is the resolution of
the system's own label of the distance
(visual_interface.cpp:304-323), and the
whole km/h is set here for each speed on
the display. The scene of the panel gives
no speed of the closest object, so the
scene that the display takes carries it
(REQ-HMI-001). The mark that the
visualization draws from AutoDrive alone
(occupancy_bridge.cpp:79-84) is no closest
object of the fusion, and the display
shows no such mark as that object.
test
Met when each of SC-HMI-001 and SC-HMI-002
has at least one run whose scenes give an
object that the system acts on, and in
each run of SC-HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007 each
frame on the display that shows a scene
shows, as an element of its own, the
object that the system acts on of that
scene when it has one and no such element
when it has none, the fixed distance of
150 m included; marks no box of the
objects and no mark of AutoDrive alone as
that object; and shows its distance as the
distance of the scene rounded to the whole
metre and its speed as the speed of the
closest object of the scene times 3.6,
rounded to the whole km/h, with its sign.
REQ-HMI-003
reqShowTheVehicleSpeed
The HMI display shall show, within the
presentation time, each vehicle speed that
reaches it, or a newer one, to the whole
km/h.
NEED-HMI-002; scope item hmiSpeedInScope;
scenarios SC-HMI-001, SC-HMI-002 and SC-
HMI-007
The driver supervises the driver-
assistance system with the same speed that
the system acts on (NEED-HMI-002). In the
realization of the driver-assistance
increment the vehicle speed enters the
system with its sample time in simulation
time, typed by COVESA VSS in km/h
(VehicleSpeedSamplePayload and MAP-
DRIVING-DA-VEHICLE-SPEED), and the system
reads it once in each result pass. The
display takes the speed of each world
snapshot that reaches the input of the
system, not the copy that the system reads
in each result pass (MAP-DRIVING-DA-
VEHICLE-SPEED): the signal is the same,
and the snapshots go on when the system
gives no result. The vehicle gives the
speed, and which element brings it to the
display is for the architecture phases
(vehicleSpeedSourceComment). The display
may skip a sample only for a newer one,
and the presentation time bounds the
delay. Before the first vehicle speed of a
run reaches the display there is no speed
to show, and REQ-HMI-006 shows the element
as outdated. In the runs of SC-HMI-003 to
SC-HMI-006, REQ-HMI-008 judges this
obligation through each outage.
test
Met when each of SC-HMI-001, SC-HMI-002
and SC-HMI-007 has at least one run, and
in each of their runs each speed on a
frame on the display is the value of a
vehicle speed of the run that has reached
the HMI display, rounded to the whole
km/h; each vehicle speed that reaches the
HMI display, or a newer one, is on the
display less than 0.1 s of wall-clock time
after it arrives; and no frame shows a
speed from another source, a fixed value
of the display's own, or a speed before
the first vehicle speed of the run reaches
the HMI display.
REQ-HMI-004
reqCollisionWarningWhileRequested
The HMI display shall give the collision
warning on the display and as a sound
while, and only while, the warning request
asks for it, each mode following each
change of the asking within the
presentation time.
NEED-HMI-003; REQ-AEBS-002;
hmiWarningSequenceConcern; scope item
hmiCollisionWarningInScope; gap
gapHmiRendererCollisionWarning; scenarios
SC-HMI-001, SC-HMI-002 and SC-HMI-007
The display gives the warning so that the
driver can act on an imminent collision,
and none without a request (NEED-HMI-003).
The warning request is the output that the
driver-assistance increment realizes from
the warnings of each plan: one event for
each plan, which asks for the collision
warning when the plan holds the forward-
collision warning or the emergency braking
and carries the capture time in simulation
time of the frame that the plan came from,
with no value changed on its path
(CollisionWarningRequestOutput and MAP-
DRIVING-DA-WARNING-REQUEST). The request
does not tell the two apart, so the
display gives one collision warning for
both. The request carries no end, so the
warning lasts while the request asks: a
continuing request continues the warning,
and the warning ends once the request asks
for none or is outdated, when REQ-HMI-007
shows that it is unavailable. Each mode
follows each change within the
presentation time that REQ-HMI-005 sets,
at the start and at the end alike. The
term takes only the form of the request,
so the requirement names no variant. It
rests on REQ-AEBS-002, the collision
warning that the product line asks for;
whether a warning is due is the decision
of the driver-assistance system, which
that increment judges. The vehicle data of
the renderer holds no collision warning
yet (gapHmiRendererCollisionWarning). In
the runs of SC-HMI-003 to SC-HMI-006, REQ-
HMI-008 judges this obligation through
each outage. No safety claim is made.
test
Met when each run of SC-HMI-001 has at
least one start of a request that reaches
the HMI display, and in each run of SC-
HMI-001, SC-HMI-002 and SC-HMI-007 each
mode of the collision warning is on from
less than 0.1 s of wall-clock time after
each start of a request reaches the HMI
display until less than 0.1 s of wall-
clock time after the warning request ends
its asking, and at no other time, with no
recording or overlay in place of either
mode.
REQ-HMI-005
reqStartEachWarningModeWithinLimit
When the start of a request reaches the
HMI display, the HMI display shall start
each mode of the collision warning within
0.1 s of wall-clock time.
NEED-HMI-003; REQ-AEBS-002;
hmiWarningSequenceConcern; gap
gapHmiWarningPresentation; scenarios SC-
HMI-001 and SC-HMI-002
This is a performance requirement on the
share of the HMI display in the time that
the driver-assistance increment allots
from the warning request to each mode.
REQ-DRIVING-042 allots 0.2 s of wall-clock
time to the Eclipse S-CORE path and the
AAOS SDV together, and the realization of
that increment divides it, on its path to
its own app on the IVI VM, into 0.1 s for
the path and 0.1 s for the presentation,
from the receipt to the first frame with
the warning and to the start of the sound
(MAP-DRIVING-DA-WARNING-REQUEST). The
boundary of the HMI display lies at the
SDV Core VM, with the Eclipse S-CORE path
outside it and the paths from the SDV Core
VM inside it, so the share of the display
starts when the start of a request reaches
it. Unlike that division, whose path share
runs to the receipt on the IVI VM, the
share of the display also holds the paths
from the SDV Core VM to the renderer and
to the app. The 0.1 s is chosen here by
analogy with that division and leaves the
other 0.1 s to the part before the
boundary. It is unmeasured for the high
availability renderer and for the sound,
and it is revisited when a readiness probe
measures them (gapHmiWarningPresentation).
Within is strict, so a mode that starts
exactly at the limit is late. A mode
starts at its start of a mode; a recording
or an overlay in place of a mode is no
start. The limit counts in wall-clock time
while the simulation runs no faster than
wall-clock time, which is the obligation
of System 2, and makes no timing claim for
a vehicle.
test
Met when each run of SC-HMI-001 has at
least one start of a request that reaches
the HMI display, and for each start of a
request that reaches the HMI display in a
run of SC-HMI-001 or SC-HMI-002, the first
frame on the display with the warning and
the start of the sound each come less than
0.1 s of wall-clock time after it arrives,
with no recording or overlay in place of
either mode.
REQ-HMI-006
reqShowOutdatedElementsAsOutdated
The HMI display shall show each element as
outdated while, and only while, the
element is outdated, following each change
of its state within the presentation time.
NEED-HMI-005; hmiContentCurrencyConcern;
scope item hmiStaleContentInScope;
scenarios SC-HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
The display shows no element as current
when it is not, so that the driver
supervises the driver-assistance system on
what it perceives now (NEED-HMI-005). The
scene and the warning request share one
period of 0.1 s of simulation time in the
realization of the driver-assistance
increment: one camera image, one result
pass, one plan and one event of the
warning request each 0.1 s; the vehicle
speed comes with each world snapshot at
the input of the system, every step of
0.05 s. The limits of the term current
take two periods, so that one late value
is tolerated. The vehicle speed brings the
newest time to the display with each world
snapshot, so the limit in simulation time
also counts the time from the capture of a
frame to the arrival of its scene and its
event at the display, and the time that
the display takes to show the scene. While
those times stay within one period
together, a scene stays current until the
next one is shown, and the warning request
until its next event; with longer times an
element can turn outdated before its next
value comes, and the limit is revisited
once a readiness probe measures them
(warningPresentationFixedInPhase5). The
limit in simulation time counts against
the newest time that has reached the
display, so it catches a delay before the
display, which an age taken from the
arrival would hide, and a value whose time
the display changes. The limit in wall-
clock time counts from the arrival of the
newest value of the input, so it catches
every input stopping, when the newest time
stops as well. Late and missing values
give one state, outdated, and phase 8
states how an outdated element looks; the
visual design stays out of scope
(hmiHumanFactorsOutOfScope). An element is
shown as current again once it is current,
which is the validity rule of the display;
the converse, current while it is current,
keeps a display from showing everything as
outdated. The state of each element counts
on its own, so a late scene leaves the
vehicle speed current. No safety claim is
made.
test
Met when each of SC-HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
has at least one run, each run of SC-
HMI-003 to SC-HMI-006 has its outage in
the IVI VM and each run of SC-HMI-007 the
stop of the Eclipse S-CORE path, and in
each run each frame on the display shows
each element as outdated, in the form that
phase 8 states for it, from less than 0.1
s of wall-clock time after the element
turns outdated until less than 0.1 s of
wall-clock time after it turns current
again, and as current at every other time;
an element is outdated from the start of
the run until a first current value of its
input reaches the HMI display.
REQ-HMI-007
reqShowWarningUnavailableWhileRequestOutdated
The HMI display shall show that the
collision warning is unavailable while,
and only while, the warning request is
outdated, following each change of the
state of the warning request within the
presentation time.
NEED-HMI-005; REQ-AEBS-013;
hmiContentCurrencyConcern; gap
gapHmiWarningAvailability; scenarios SC-
HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
The display shows when the warning is
unavailable, so that the driver can tell a
warning that cannot come from one that is
not due (NEED-HMI-005); it rests on
N-AEBS-008, that the availability of the
AEBS be apparent, and on the status
indication of REQ-AEBS-013. This is the
one degraded response of the set. The
warning request carries no indication of
its own availability
(gapHmiWarningAvailability), and one of
its events comes for each plan, telling
whether it asks, so the display learns
from their age that the warning cannot
come: the warning is unavailable while the
warning request is outdated. A signal of
its own would need a change of the driver-
assistance system
(hmiCandidateChangeOutOfScope). The
warning shows as available again once the
warning request is current, which is the
validity rule; the converse keeps a
display from showing the warning as
unavailable at all times. In SC-HMI-007
the Eclipse S-CORE path ends carrying the
request, and the display shows the warning
as unavailable while the driver still sees
the vehicle speed. A renderer that cannot
give the warning, such as a sound output
that is out, is left for a later increment
(warningAvailabilityFixedInPhase5). No
safety claim is made.
test
Met when each of SC-HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
has at least one run, each run of SC-
HMI-007 has the stop of the Eclipse S-CORE
path at least 0.3 s of wall-clock time
before its end, and in each run the
display shows that the collision warning
is unavailable from less than 0.1 s of
wall-clock time after the warning request
turns outdated until less than 0.1 s of
wall-clock time after it turns current
again, and at no other time, so that the
warning shows as available again only once
an event of the warning request is
current.
REQ-HMI-008
reqSpeedAndWarningThroughOutages
Throughout each outage in the IVI VM, the
HMI display shall show the vehicle speed,
give the collision warning while the
warning request asks for it, and show that
the warning is unavailable while the
warning request is outdated.
NEED-HMI-004; REQ-AEBS-013;
hmiAndroidOutageConcern; scope item
hmiAndroidOutageInScope; scenarios SC-
HMI-003 to SC-HMI-006
While the drawing of the scene or Android
in the IVI VM is out, the driver-
assistance system goes on driving the
vehicle, and the driver still needs the
speed and the warning, or to know that the
warning cannot come (NEED-HMI-004). The
outages are those of the story: the app
that draws the scene ends or hangs (SC-
HMI-003), and Android in the IVI VM boots
(SC-HMI-004), hangs (SC-HMI-005) or
restarts (SC-HMI-006). REQ-HMI-003, REQ-
HMI-004, REQ-HMI-005 and REQ-HMI-007 state
the speed and the warning in every run;
this requirement carries them through each
outage, and its criteria judge them there.
It rests on N-AEBS-008 and on the status
indication of REQ-AEBS-013. Each outage is
an event inside the boundary of the
display, whose detection phases 6 to 8
decide (guestAcrossBoundaryComment). The
speed and the warning hold throughout, the
scene returns under REQ-HMI-001 once the
app gives frames again, and until then
REQ-HMI-006 shows it as outdated, within
the limits of the term current and the
presentation time from the last scene that
the app has shown. No time from a restart
to the scene is set here; that limit, and
whether the HMI display meets those of
REQ-HMI-006 through a hang of the app or
of Android in the IVI VM, stay open with
the owner until a probe measures them. No
safety claim is made.
test
Met when each of SC-HMI-003 to SC-HMI-006
has at least one run, each run has its
outage in the IVI VM with at least one
start of a request reaching the HMI
display during it, and throughout the
outage of each run each frame on the
display and each mode of the collision
warning meet what the criteria of REQ-
HMI-003, REQ-HMI-004, REQ-HMI-005 and REQ-
HMI-007 ask of them.
REQ-HMI-009
reqRendererSplitAndInputPaths
The HMI display shall draw the vehicle
speed and the collision warning and give
its sound by the high availability
renderer in an SDV Media VM, and draw the
scene by an app in the IVI VM, each taking
its inputs from the SDV Core VM over paths
inside the boundary of the HMI display.
NEED-HMI-004;
hmiRendererAllocationConcern;
hmiRendererPathConcern; scope item
hmiRendererSplitInScope; gaps
gapHmiRendererIntegration and
gapHmiMemberGuestLayout
This is a design constraint on the
realization of the HMI display, from the
owner's decision of 2026-11-17: the high
availability renderer in an SDV Media VM
draws the speed and the collision warning
and gives its sound, and an app in the IVI
VM draws the scene, so that the speed and
the warning do not depend on Android in
the IVI VM (hmiRendererSplitInScope). The
boundary puts the paths from the SDV Core
VM inside the display and the Eclipse
S-CORE path outside it. How a collision
warning and its sound reach the renderer
is open (gapHmiRendererCollisionWarning),
and so is how the renderer and the guest
fit a bench (gapHmiRendererIntegration).
Phases 6 to 8 decide the elements on each
path and how the app tells the renderer
that Android is alive; this requirement
fixes only the split and that the paths
stay inside the boundary. It names the
AAOS SDV guest, and phase 9 links it.
inspect
Met when the inspection of the realization
that phase 8 records shows the vehicle
speed, the collision warning on the
display and its sound in the high
availability renderer in an SDV Media VM,
the scene in an app in the IVI VM, and for
each input the elements that carry it from
the SDV Core VM to the renderer or to the
app, all inside the boundary of the HMI
display, with no other element drawing the
vehicle speed or the collision warning.
REQ-HMI-010
reqRecordDisplayIdentity
The HMI display shall record its display
identity before its first frame on the
display in each run.
NEED-HMI-006; hmiDisplayVerdictConcern;
scope item hmiVerdictEvidenceInScope;
assumption asmHmiSimulationStandsIn;
scenarios SC-HMI-001 to SC-HMI-007
A verdict holds only for the display that
ran, and the configuration of the display
is every setting that it reads at its
start (NEED-HMI-006). The parts of the
identity are pinned each on its own,
because none of them fixes the others: the
build of each of the two drawing elements,
the image of each guest VM, the sound of
the warning, the files of the
configuration and the settings of the
start. Each part is the SHA-256 of named
files or a setting written out, so that
another engineer can check it. The
candidate revision is bound by the run of
the driver-assistance system (NEED-
DRIVING-011 and REQ-DRIVING-044), and the
record of what that system gives, the
captures and the evaluators belong to
System 2 and are bound there. Like REQ-
DRIVING-044, the record is a behaviour of
the display in each run, which phase 6
allocates to a function. A verdict holds
for the simulated configuration only
(asmHmiSimulationStandsIn).
test
Met when every run of SC-HMI-001 to SC-
HMI-007 has the record of its display
identity before its first frame on the
display; when another engineer who hashes
the named files obtains the recorded
values; and when a display with one
changed build, image, sound file,
configuration file or start setting
records a different display identity.
